topic: How Transformers Store Facts: The MLP as a Key-Value Memory
target_audience: University students in Computer Science or AI enthusiasts with basic linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Mystery: Where are the Facts?
sections.content: Introduction to the Transformer architecture. While Attention handles relationships between words, the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layers act as the 'long-term memory' storage where factual knowledge resides.
sections.example: Visual: A brain icon splitting into two parts. Left (Attention) focuses on grammar; Right (MLP) holds a library of facts like 'The capital of France is Paris'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Dot Products as Similarity
sections.content: A brief review of vector dot products. If two vectors point in the same direction, their dot product is high. This is the mathematical 'searching' mechanism used to find a fact.
sections.example: Animation: Two vectors A and B. As the angle between them shrinks, a 'Match Score' bar fills up. This represents the model recognizing a specific concept.

sections.title: The First Layer: The Key Detectors
sections.content: The first linear layer of the MLP acts as a set of 'Keys' or 'Detectors'. Each neuron represents a specific pattern or concept. When the input vector matches a 'Key', the neuron fires (Activation).
sections.example: Visual: An input vector 'Eiffel Tower' passes through a filter. Only the neuron labeled 'French Landmarks' glows brightly while others remain dim.

sections.title: The Second Layer: The Value Retrievers
sections.content: The second linear layer acts as 'Values'. Once a 'Key' neuron is activated, it triggers a corresponding 'Value' vector to be added to the model's current understanding. This is the 'fact' being retrieved.
sections.example: Graphical Concept: The glowing 'French Landmarks' neuron pushes out a vector representing the word 'Paris'. Mathematically: Output = Activation * Value_Vector.

sections.title: The Full Pipeline: Fact Retrieval in Action
sections.content: Integrating the two layers into the Key-Value Memory framework. The MLP performs a 'Soft Lookup' where it can combine multiple facts simultaneously if the input is complex.
sections.example: Character Example: A robot librarian receives the query 'Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?'. It activates the 'Shakespeare' key, which retrieves the 'Playwright' value, resulting in the correct output.

sections.title: Scaling Up: Billions of Memories
sections.content: Conclusion on why Transformers are so large. Each MLP layer contains thousands of these Key-Value pairs. Across 96 layers (like in GPT-3), the model stores a massive web of human knowledge.
sections.example: Visual: Zooming out from one MLP neuron to a grid of millions, showing how they form a massive 'Knowledge Map' inside the GPU memory.
